**1. SCOPE OF WORK**

The work order for Maintenance Work Order 2025-0147 describes its scope_description as Replacement of timber transoms and rail fastenings on Pindar Bridge. Record status: current.

The full scope of this work order is the replacement of timber transoms and rail fastenings on Pindar Bridge, located on the Geraldton–Northam line approximately 4.5 km south of the Pindar siding and 28 km north of Mullewa. The bridge carries a single mainline track over a seasonal creek. The existing transoms are assessed as life-expired, with evidence of rot in the end zones and significant fastener deterioration. The replacement transoms will be installed to the current standard drawings, and all rail fastenings will be replaced with new galvanised components to match the new transom drillings.

The scope was derived from RSIR-2025-06, the structural inspection report prepared by WRTA Bridge Inspection in June 2025, and includes the following principal activities:

a) Removal of existing timber transoms and associated fastenings, including disposal of removed material in accordance with WRTA environmental procedures.

b) Supply and installation of new H4-treated hardwood transoms, 300 x 300 x 4200 mm, to the dimensions and drillings shown on the standard drawings.

c) Supply and installation of new rail fastenings, including galvanised coach screws, strap assemblies, and all associated washers and nuts.

d) Field treatment of all cuts, drillings, and abrasions to the new transoms using copper naphthenate, in accordance with the timber treatment specification.

e) Re-installation of the existing guard rails and any bridge-mounted signage disturbed during the works.

f) Removal of all plant, equipment, and surplus material from site, and reinstatement of any disturbed access tracks or surrounds.

The scope does not include replacement of the bridge girders, deck plating, or any concrete substructure elements. Any defects identified in these components during the course of the works are to be reported to the WRTA Bridge Engineer for separate assessment.

## 1. SCOPE OF WORK

The scope of this work order covers the replacement of transoms on the Pindar Bridge structure as identified in the most recent bridge inspection report (ref. BIR-2025-088). The works include, but are not limited to:

- Removal and disposal of existing transoms identified as defective or end-of-life.
- Supply and installation of new transoms (hardwood, species – Jarrah, preservative treated) to match existing geometry and fastening configuration.
- Installation of new fastening assemblies (screws, bolts, washers, and baseplates) as specified in the approved standard drawing set (ref. SD-214-07 Rev C).
- Re-alignment and re-fastening of the continuous welded rail (CWR) across the bridge deck.
- Replacement of ballast and re-profiling on bridge approaches (25 m either side of abutments).
- Removal of redundant and obsolete fittings and disposal off-site.
- Reinstatement of any disturbed track drainage.
- Site cleanup and restoration of any disturbed areas outside the track corridor.

The works shall be undertaken in accordance with the following key documents (latest revision unless noted):

## 2. WORK METHOD OVERVIEW

A summary of the proposed sequence of works is provided below. Detailed step-by-step procedures are contained in the endorsed Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS) referenced above.

1. **Site establishment and induction:** Establish site compound, set up traffic management at access points, and conduct site induction for all personnel.
2. **Pre-works inspection and survey:** Confirm transom positions, rail geometry, and fastener locations against the approved drawings. Record any discrepancies and notify the Project Engineer prior to commencing removal works.
3. **Rail support and clipping:** Install rail support stands and release fastenings as required to allow safe removal of transoms. Comply with all requirements for CWR stress management.
4. **Transom removal:** Remove defective transoms using approved lifting methods. Handle removed materials carefully to avoid damage to adjacent components.
5. **Transom installation:** Install new transoms, position and align to tolerance, then secure with approved fastening assemblies.
6. **Rail re-fastening and alignment:** Re-fasten rail, adjust geometry to within tolerances specified in MRS-SP-022, and verify stress-free temperature (SFT) compliance.
7. **Ballast works:** Place, profile, and consolidate ballast on bridge approaches as specified.
8. **Inspection and verification:** Conduct a joint inspection with the Project Engineer and the asset owner's representative. Complete all required checklists and handover documentation.
9. **Site cleanup and demobilisation:** Remove all plant, equipment, and materials from site. Reinstate any disturbed areas.

**1. SCOPE OF WORK**

The work order for Maintenance Work Order 2025-0147 describes its scope_description as Replacement of timber transoms and rail fastenings on Pindar Bridge. Record status: current.

The full scope of this work order is the replacement of timber transoms and rail fastenings on Pindar Bridge, located on the Geraldton–Northam line approximately 4.5 km south of the Pindar siding and 28 km north of Mullewa. The bridge carries a single mainline track over a seasonal creek. The existing transoms are assessed as life-expired, with evidence of rot in the end zones and significant fastener deterioration. The replacement transoms will be installed to the current standard drawings, and all rail fastenings will be replaced with new galvanised components to match the new transom drillings.

The scope was derived from RSIR-2025-06, the structural inspection report prepared by WRTA Bridge Inspection in June 2025, and includes the following principal activities:

a) Removal of existing timber transoms and associated fastenings, including disposal of removed material in accordance with WRTA environmental procedures.

b) Supply and installation of new H4-treated hardwood transoms, 300 x 300 x 4200 mm, to the dimensions and drillings shown on the standard drawings.

c) Supply and installation of new rail fastenings, including galvanised coach screws, strap assemblies, and all associated washers and nuts.

d) Field treatment of all cuts, drillings, and abrasions to the new transoms using copper naphthenate, in accordance with the timber treatment specification.

e) Re-installation of the existing guard rails and any bridge-mounted signage disturbed during the works.

f) Removal of all plant, equipment, and surplus material from site, and reinstatement of any disturbed access tracks or surrounds.

The scope does not include replacement of the bridge girders, deck plating, or any concrete substructure elements. Any defects identified in these components during the course of the works are to be reported to the WRTA Bridge Engineer for separate assessment.

- The bridge is approximately 12 km from Mullewa and 8 km from Pindar siding. Local services (fuel, water, accommodation) are not available at the site; the contractor is to make their own arrangements.
- Mobile phone reception at the site is limited. The contractor is to provide a suitable means of communication (e.g., satellite phone or UHF radio) for the duration of the works.
- The site is in an area of remnant native vegetation. Disturbance is to be limited to the existing access tracks and the immediate works area. No clearing of vegetation is permitted without prior approval from the WRTA Environment Officer.

## 1. SCOPE OF WORK

The scope of this work order covers the replacement of transoms on the Pindar Bridge structure as identified in the most recent bridge inspection report (ref. BIR-2025-088). The works include, but are not limited to:

- Removal and disposal of existing transoms identified as defective or end-of-life.
- Supply and installation of new transoms (hardwood, species – Jarrah, preservative treated) to match existing geometry and fastening configuration.
- Installation of new fastening assemblies (screws, bolts, washers, and baseplates) as specified in the approved standard drawing set (ref. SD-214-07 Rev C).
- Re-alignment and re-fastening of the continuous welded rail (CWR) across the bridge deck.
- Replacement of ballast and re-profiling on bridge approaches (25 m either side of abutments).
- Removal of redundant and obsolete fittings and disposal off-site.
- Reinstatement of any disturbed track drainage.
- Site cleanup and restoration of any disturbed areas outside the track corridor.

The works shall be undertaken in accordance with the following key documents (latest revision unless noted):

| Document No. | Title |
|---|---|
| MRS-SP-022 | Track Resurfacing and Ballast Profiling Specification |
| MRS-SP-041 | Bridge Timber Component Supply and Installation Specification |
| MRS-SP-055 | Possession Management and Site Safety Requirements |
| MRS-SW-118 | Safe Work Method Statement – Bridge Transom Replacement (to be reviewed and endorsed for this work order) |
| SD-214-07 Rev C | Standard Drawing – Pindar Bridge Deck and Transom Details |

---

## 2. WORK METHOD OVERVIEW

A summary of the proposed sequence of works is provided below. Detailed step-by-step procedures are contained in the endorsed Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS) referenced above.

1. **Site establishment and induction:** Establish site compound, set up traffic management at access points, and conduct site induction for all personnel.
2. **Pre-works inspection and survey:** Confirm transom positions, rail geometry, and fastener locations against the approved drawings. Record any discrepancies and notify the Project Engineer prior to commencing removal works.
3. **Rail support and clipping:** Install rail support stands and release fastenings as required to allow safe removal of transoms. Comply with all requirements for CWR stress management.
4. **Transom removal:** Remove defective transoms using approved lifting methods. Handle removed materials carefully to avoid damage to adjacent components.
5. **Transom installation:** Install new transoms, position and align to tolerance, then secure with approved fastening assemblies.
6. **Rail re-fastening and alignment:** Re-fasten rail, adjust geometry to within tolerances specified in MRS-SP-022, and verify stress-free temperature (SFT) compliance.
7. **Ballast works:** Place, profile, and consolidate ballast on bridge approaches as specified.
8. **Inspection and verification:** Conduct a joint inspection with the Project Engineer and the asset owner's representative. Complete all required checklists and handover documentation.
9. **Site cleanup and demobilisation:** Remove all plant, equipment, and materials from site. Reinstate any disturbed areas.

d) Vehicle access to the bridge site shall be via the existing service road off the Pindar–Yalgoo Road. Vehicles must not be driven on the track formation or within 3 metres of the outer rail unless authorised by the Possession Manager.

e) No unauthorised access to the bridge structure will be permitted. All persons accessing the bridge structure must hold the appropriate competency for working at heights and must be listed on the site access register.

4. POSSESSION BOUNDARIES

The possession notice for Track Possession Notice TPN-2025-118 states its possession_start_datetime as 2025-09-14T22:00:00+08:00. Record status: current.

The possession applies to the track between the following limits:

a) From signal SG-214.5 (Mullewa end) to signal SG-214.7 (Pindar end), inclusive of all tracks within these limits.

b) The possession includes the full width of the rail corridor at Pindar Bridge, including the bridge structure, abutments, and any temporary works areas established in accordance with the Work Order Environmental Management Plan.

c) The possession does not include the adjacent track at any location. The adjacent track remains open to rail traffic and must be kept clear of all persons, plant and materials.

d) Where the possession is adjacent to an open track, a physical barrier or distance limit must be maintained in accordance with POTW-2024.

5. HAZARDS AND SITE CONDITIONS

The following hazards have been identified for the works area. The Possession Manager shall ensure these are communicated to all persons on site prior to the commencement of any work.

a) Overhead wiring is present at the location and must be treated as live unless a certificate of isolation (Form EI-1) has been issued in accordance with WRTA Electrical Safety Procedure EP-08.

b) Pindar Creek runs beneath the bridge. Water levels may rise rapidly following rainfall in the catchment. The Possession Manager shall monitor weather conditions and cease work in the creek bed if water levels begin to rise.

c) The bridge structure may contain asbestos materials in the original decking. A licensed asbestos assessor must inspect any material suspected of containing asbestos prior to disturbance. The Work Order Environmental Management Plan includes the asbestos register for the structure.

d) The area is known habitat for the Western Spiny-tailed Skink. A fauna spotter-catcher must be present during any ground-disturbing activities within 20 metres of the creek line.

6. GENERAL CONDITIONS AND SAFETY PRECAUTIONS

All persons entering the possession shall comply with the following conditions. The Possession Manager is responsible for ensuring that these conditions are communicated and understood by all persons under their control prior to the commencement of any work.

a) A safe system of work must be in place and documented prior to any activity commencing within the possession. The safe system of work must be approved by the Possession Manager and must include a job safety analysis for each discrete work activity.

b) All persons entering the possession must hold a current track access permit or be accompanied by a person who holds such a permit. Proof of competency must be available for inspection upon request by an authorised WRTA officer.

c) Personal protective equipment must be worn at all times within the possession. Minimum requirements are high visibility clothing, safety footwear, and a safety helmet. Additional PPE requirements are specified in the Work Order Environmental Management Plan and the relevant job safety analyses.

d) No person shall enter the possession without first signing on at the possession control point. Signing off must occur upon leaving the possession. The Possession Manager shall maintain a record of all persons entering and leaving the possession and shall reconcile this record at the completion of each shift.

e) Mobile plant and equipment must not be operated within 3 metres of the open adjacent track unless a physical barrier or distance limit has been established in accordance with POTW-2024. Where plant is required to operate within this distance, a spotter must be appointed and the operation must be approved by the Possession Manager.

f) All tools, materials, and equipment must be secured or removed from the possession at the completion of each shift. No materials may be left within 2 metres of the open adjacent track overnight without the approval of the Possession Manager.

g) The speed limit for any rail traffic operating on the adjacent open track is not affected by this possession. The Possession Manager shall ensure that no activity causes any obstruction, encroachment, or distraction to rail traffic on the adjacent track.

h) Hand signalling and lookout working is not permitted within this possession. All movements of persons and plant within the possession must be coordinated through the Possession Manager.

i) Any excavation or ground-disturbing activity must be undertaken in accordance with the Work Order Environmental Management Plan and the WRTA Code of Practice for Excavation. Dial Before You Dig enquiries must be completed prior to any excavation, and the relevant clearances obtained.

j) A pre-work briefing must be conducted by the Possession Manager at the commencement of each shift. The briefing shall cover the scope of work for the shift, any changes to site conditions, emergency procedures, and the location of the possession control point.

k) No alcohol or non-prescription drugs are permitted within the possession. Any person found to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs shall be removed from the possession and reported in accordance with WRTA policy.

l) The Possession Manager shall maintain a possession log recording all significant events, including weather conditions, any incidents or near misses, any changes to the scope of work, and the times of commencement and cessation of work each day.

7. SIGNALLING ARRANGEMENTS

The following signalling arrangements apply to this possession:

a) The protecting signals SG-214.5 and SG-214.7 will be placed at danger and secured in accordance with the WRTA Signalling Arrangements for Possessions procedure.

TRACK POSSESSION NOTICE TPN-2025-118 – PINDAR BRIDGE
Work Order: MWO-2025-0147
Issued by: Westland Regional Transport Authority (WRTA)

8. HANDOVER AND POSSESSION HAND-BACK PROCEDURES

The handover of the possession from the Contractor to the WRTA Possession Manager, and the
subsequent hand-back of the rail corridor to operational traffic, shall be conducted in
accordance with this section. The Contractor's Site Supervisor and the WRTA Possession Manager
are jointly responsible for ensuring that all hand-back milestones are completed before the
possession is surrendered.

The hand-back process is divided into two stages:

Stage 1 – Contractor to WRTA Possession Manager (internal handover)
Stage 2 – WRTA Possession Manager to Rail Traffic (line reopening)

Neither stage may be commenced until the preceding stage has been formally completed and
documented. The possession may not be surrendered in part; the entire possession length must be
handed back as a single unit unless otherwise agreed in writing by the WRTA Network Controller.

8.1 Hand-back Milestones and Responsible Parties

The following table lists the required hand-back milestones, the responsible party for each
milestone, and the evidence required to demonstrate completion. All milestones must be
completed in the sequence shown.

| Milestone | Description | Responsible Party | Evidence of Completion |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| M1 | All tools, plant, and materials removed from the possession and the adjacent track corridor | Contractor Site Supervisor | Completed removal checklist (Form WRTA-F-221) signed by Contractor Site Supervisor |
| M2 | All personnel accounted for and no persons remaining within the possession | Contractor Site Supervisor | Head count sheet and sign-out register |
| M3 | All temporary works, including scaffolding, falsework, and temporary shoring, dismantled and removed | Contractor Site Supervisor | Dismantling completion certificate (Form WRTA-F-223) |
| M4 | Track geometry, gauge, and alignment verified as compliant with WRTA Track Standard TS-104 | WRTA Track Inspector | Track inspection report (Form WRTA-F-118) |
| M5 | All fastenings, clips, and fishplates re-tensioned and torqued to specification | Contractor Site Supervisor | Torque test log signed by WRTA Track Inspector |
| M6 | Ballast profile restored to standard and any excess ballast removed from sleepers and rail seat | Contractor Site Supervisor | Visual inspection sign-off by WRTA Track Inspector |
| M7 | Drainage works inspected and confirmed clear of debris and obstructions | Contractor Site Supervisor | Drainage inspection record (Form WRTA-F-119) |
| M8 | All temporary speed restrictions signage and warning boards removed | WRTA Possession Manager | Signage removal register |
| M9 | Any temporary fencing removed and permanent fencing restored to pre-works condition | Contractor Site Supervisor | Fencing inspection report |
| M10 | Final joint inspection of the full possession length conducted by Contractor and WRTA | Contractor Site Supervisor and WRTA Possession Manager | Joint inspection report (Form WRTA-F-225) signed by both parties |
| M11 | Possession log closed out and all entries verified | WRTA Possession Manager | Completed possession log |
| M12 | Written confirmation provided to WRTA Network Controller that the possession is ready for surrender | WRTA Possession Manager | Hand-back notification form (Form WRTA-F-226) |

8.2 Hand-back Inspection Requirements

The final joint inspection (Milestone M10) must be conducted over the full length of the
possession. The inspection must cover:

a) The condition of the track, including rail, sleepers, fastenings, and ballast.
